sources: Most decimal fractions are approximated in binary floating point rather than represented exactly.
Typical Python floats map to IEEE-754 binary64 with 53 bits of precision.
Each floating operation can introduce a new rounding error.
repr preserves a round-trip representation of the stored float value.
float.hex and float.fromhex provide exact hexadecimal round-trip serialization.
Display rounding must not be confused with changing the stored binary value.
math.isfinite rejects both infinities and NaN.
math.nextafter exposes adjacent representable floating values.
math.ulp exposes the least-significant-bit spacing at a floating value.
math.isnan identifies NaN independently of infinity.
math.isinf identifies positive and negative infinity.
math.fsum is designed to reduce precision loss in summation but height difference itself remains a direct subtraction.
numpy.finfo reports machine limits for a selected floating dtype.
For binary64, epsilon is approximately 2.22e-16 around one.
finfo precision and resolution are dtype-specific rather than universal constants.
Subnormal values exist below the smallest normal value and can have reduced precision.
longdouble representation varies by platform, so it is not a portable terminal arithmetic contract.
Terminal arithmetic therefore pins an explicit dtype rather than inheriting platform extended precision.
numpy.nextafter returns the next representable value toward a specified direction.
nextafter can construct one-ULP lower and upper probes around an extrema or difference value.
Adjacent-value probes are dtype dependent and must use the same terminal dtype.
A nextafter bracket is diagnostic provenance, not a license to tolerance-merge distinct extrema.
Neighbor probes can detect a one-representable-step drift between replays.
Second-pass nextafter brackets must reproduce when source values and dtype are unchanged.
numpy.subtract performs element-wise x1 minus x2.
np.subtract is equivalent to the ndarray minus operator for the same inputs.
The output dtype can be controlled explicitly rather than left implicit.
Broadcasting exists and is therefore prohibited for the scalar terminal height-difference pair.
The terminal formula is maximum physical elevation minus minimum physical elevation.
Reversed subtraction is a diagnostic sign check and cannot be reported as height difference.
NumPy floating-point invalid, divide, overflow and underflow behavior is configurable.
The default invalid/divide/overflow behavior is warning rather than fail-closed.
Terminal arithmetic can explicitly set numerical exceptions to raise instead of silently continuing.
Error handling may be scoped with an explicit context.
Overflow and invalid arithmetic are distinct conditions and require separate ledger fields.
Underflow policy must be recorded even though metre-scale elevations should not approach subnormal magnitude.
NumPy defines distinct positive zero and negative zero floating representations.
npy_signbit can distinguish the sign bit including negative zero.
IEEE-style NaN is not suitable for ordinary equality-based membership checks.
Infinity classification is independent of NaN classification.
Signed-zero normalization can be serialized separately from numeric equality.
numpy.nanmin ignores NaNs when computing a minimum.
An all-NaN slice produces a warning and NaN rather than a valid minimum.
NaN-ignoring reduction is diagnostic only after explicit nodata/mask validity has been resolved.
Terminal minima must remain bound to the explicit valid-pixel set rather than inferred from NaN conventions.
A masked valid set and nanmin result can be compared as a parity diagnostic.
All-NaN target membership is a fail-closed no-elevation state.
numpy.nanmax ignores NaNs when computing a maximum.
An all-NaN slice produces a warning and NaN rather than a valid maximum.
NaN-ignoring maximum is diagnostic only after explicit raster validity semantics are established.
Terminal maxima must preserve all exact tied members rather than only the first argmax.
A masked valid set and nanmax result can be compared as a parity diagnostic.
Nonfinite maxima are rejected before subtraction.
GDAL raster bands have explicit data types, optional nodata, scale, offset and unit metadata.
Scale and offset transform stored raster samples into meaningful physical values.
Raster unit metadata can identify linear elevation units.
Stored minimum and maximum metadata are optional and not proof of a fresh exhaustive scan.
STATISTICS_APPROXIMATE identifies approximate rather than exact statistics.
Terminal arithmetic therefore uses fully scanned valid physical extrema rather than cached statistics.
GDAL multidimensional arrays define unscaled value as offset plus scale times raw value.
GDAL multidimensional arrays can carry unit, nodata, offset and scale properties.
Overviews have smaller dimensions while covering the same domain.
Terminal vertical difference excludes overview-derived extrema.
Unit and scale provenance must travel with the value array before arithmetic.
Raw-value equality is not sufficient when scale or offset metadata differs.
EA requires absolute height error below +/-15cm RMSE.
EA FAQ describes expected relative/random height error as no more than +/-5cm.
EA directs users to survey-specific Ground Truth results for a particular survey.
Generic EA accuracy statements are source specifications rather than measured target-parcel accuracy.
The 15cm RMSE and 5cm relative/random statements are distinct accuracy components.
Neither component alone establishes a confidence interval for a computed parcel height difference.
EA Ground Truth points have stated +/-3cm RMSE accuracy.
Ground Truth records include survey date, surface type, survey method, transformation and geoidal models.
Timestamped LIDAR QC compares RMSE, standard deviation and random error against Ground Truth.
EA Ground Truth dataset states 10cm standard deviation/random error for QC pass.
The Ground Truth 10cm QC statement conflicts numerically with the separate FAQ 5cm expected random-error statement.
That 5cm/10cm conflict remains explicit until the selected survey's own QC metadata is bound.
OS states OSGM15 Great Britain height standard error is 0.008m.
OSGM15 standard error excludes GNSS heighting errors.
OSGM15 height errors vary by regional vertical datum.
The 0.008m value is a transformation-model component, not target LIDAR measurement accuracy.
OS Net height accuracy is a separate component from OSGM15 transformation accuracy.
OSGM15 error must not be silently root-sum-squared with EA RMSE without a supported uncertainty model.
candidates: Height difference equals max minus min
No unrelated division in terminal arithmetic
Terminal vertical arithmetic and accuracy provenance bundle
terminal_policy: Use exact finite physical extrema after scale/offset/unit/datum validation; pin Float64 arithmetic; compute max-minus-min without pre-rounding; serialize repr+hex+ULP/nextafter provenance; reject NaN/Inf/all-NaN; keep EA RMSE/random-error/Ground-Truth and OSGM15 components separate; do not invent combined RMSE, confidence interval, or measured target accuracy.
